title: Logspace decidability of circuit scan languages
statement: Let $C$ be a family of Boolean circuits and let $f$ map bit strings to bit strings. Suppose $f$ has output length bounded by a polynomial in the input length, and both languages asking whether the $i$th output bit of $f(x)$ is true and whether $i$ is less than the length of $f(x)$ are decidable in logarithmic space. Suppose also that, for every $n$, $f(1^n)$ is the encoding of the $n$th circuit in $C$. Then, for each scan task—testing circuit size indices, vertex types, or edges—the corresponding language of encoded queries is decidable in logarithmic space.
hypotheses_covered: The output-bit index language for $f$ is in LOGSPACE
The output-length index language for $f$ is in LOGSPACE
